title: Ledgerline: AKS, Azure SQL, Service Bus, Key Vault, Azure DevOps
proves: The runbook goes to Common Failures, not Security; the 'Never rotate' rule goes to Danger Zones.
transcript:
Thanks for joining. This handover covers Ledgerline, the invoicing platform our finance customers use to bill about four thousand businesses.
Ledgerline runs on Azure Kubernetes Service in West Europe. The API and the PDF worker are separate deployments in the billing namespace.
Invoices are stored in Azure SQL Database, files go to Blob Storage, and we use Azure Service Bus to queue invoice generation jobs. Redis is Azure Cache for Redis.
Infrastructure is Terraform, and Azure DevOps pipelines deploy with Helm. Production deploys need two approvals and only run on Tuesday or Thursday mornings.
Monitoring is Azure Monitor with Application Insights. The alert that matters is queue depth on Service Bus above five thousand messages.
When invoices get stuck, check whether the PDF worker pods are in CrashLoopBackOff; usually the Key Vault secret for the signing certificate expired. Renew it in Key Vault and restart the worker.
Secrets live in Key Vault and pods read them through workload identity. Never rotate the SQL admin password without telling the finance on-call first.
Geo-replication to North Europe is configured. RPO is fifteen minutes and RTO is one hour, and we test failover every quarter.
The platform team owns the cluster; we own the application. Priya Nair is the escalation contact after thirty minutes.
Month end is the busiest time, so no changes in the last three days of the month.
